questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers from amongst the given options should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14
questions.solution:
The pattern  followed here is:

Find which two number from the among the given options should be interchanged to make the given equation correct.

Let's check each option one by one:

Option 1) 78 and 216

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 78 ÷ ( 216 × 1 - 8) = 14

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 78 ÷ 208 = 14

⇒ 42 + 0.375 = 14

⇒ 42.375 ≠ 14 

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 14 and 8

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 14) = 8

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ 64 = 8

⇒ 42 + 3.375 = 8

⇒ 45.375 ≠ 8 

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 78 and 14

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ (14 × 1 - 8) = 78

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ 6 = 78

⇒ 42 + 36 = 78

⇒ 78 = 78

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) 216 and 168

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 216 ÷ 4 + 168 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

⇒ 216 ÷ 4 + 168 ÷ 70 = 14

⇒ 54 + 2.4 = 14

⇒ 56.4 ≠ 14

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

⇒8.94 ≠ 12. 

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS. (Incorrect)

⇒ 4 × 8 + 7 - 2 = 37

⇒ 32 + 7 - 2 = 37

⇒ 39 - 2 = 37

⇒ 37 = 37

⇒ LHS = RHS (Correct)

⇒ 9 - 7 × 3 + 6 × 4 ÷ 1 = 12

⇒ 9 - 7 × 3 + 6 × 4 = 12

⇒ 9 - 21 + 24 = 12

⇒ 33 - 21 = 12

⇒ 12 = 12

⇒ LHS = RHS. (Correct)

Option 4) 4 × 8 - 9 ÷ 3 + 7 = 57

Given: 7 and 4

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 7 × 8 - 9 ÷ 3 + 4 = 57

⇒ 7 × 8 - 3 + 4 = 57

⇒ 56 - 3 + 4 = 57

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. Back in April P. an afternoon walking around Q. the Tillman Sand Ridge Heritage Preserve R. I was visiting family in South Carolina S. and my brother and I spent
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Back in April

P. an afternoon walking around

Q. the Tillman Sand Ridge Heritage Preserve

R. I was visiting family in South Carolina

S. and my brother and I spent
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'RSPQ'.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting off a story, starting of an incident or an event, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
  • The reason for this order is that the sentence begins with the context of the speaker visiting family in South Carolina (R).
  • Then, the speaker mentions spending an afternoon walking around (P) and specifies the location as the Tillman Sand Ridge Heritage Preserve (Q).
  • Finally, the sentence ends by mentioning the speaker's brother being there with them (S). 
  • Thus, the correct sequence will be:
    • R. I was visiting family in South Carolina
    • S. And my brother and I spent
    • P. An afternoon walking around
    • Q. The Tillman Sand Ridge Heritage Preserve
       

Correct Sequence: I was visiting family in South Carolina and my brother and I spent an afternoon walking around the Tillman Sand Ridge Heritage Preserve.

  • The given sentence is an example of 'past continuous'. 
  • The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
    • Subject + was/were + V1+ing + Object. (Active Voice)

    • Here, in the given sentence 'was writing' will be changed into 'was being written'. 
    • 'A letter' will be changed into the subject.

    • The preposition 'by' will be added. 
       

​Correct Sentence: A letter was being written by Sudha to her husband.
